## Purpose

`bardo-golem` is the single binary entry point for the Bardo runtime. It initializes the async environment, sets up observability with tracing, and orchestrates startup of subsystems (Heartbeat, Grimoire, Safety, Mortality, etc.). Currently a shell; later plans implement the full startup sequence and subsystem coordination.

## Key Invariants

- Tokio runtime must be initialized via `#[tokio::main]` attribute
- `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()` must be called exactly once, before any logging or subsystem initialization
- `main()` returns `anyhow::Result<()>` to propagate startup errors and context upward
- Binary name in Cargo.toml `[[bin]]` section (`bardo-golem`) matches the executable name
- No `src/lib.rs` exists; this is a binary-only crate

## Public API

This is a binary crate. It provides:

- **`bardo-golem` executable** — the runtime entry point; started by user or orchestrator to begin a Golem instance

(Currently: tracing initialization and placeholder main.)

## Dependencies

- `tokio` (workspace) — async runtime; multithread executor for concurrent I/O
- `tracing` (workspace) — structured logging facade
- `tracing-subscriber` (workspace) — fmt formatter for console output
- `anyhow` (workspace) — error context and Result propagation

## Implementation Notes

- This crate exports no public types. Subsystems are imported from other crates (golem-core, golem-grimoire, etc.) by future startup code.
- The `#[tokio::main]` attribute expands to create and block on a Runtime. Do not wrap main in another runtime call.
- Tracing initialization must happen once at startup. Calling `fmt::init()` a second time will panic.
- Future startup sequence will likely be: (1) tracing init (done), (2) load config from disk (golem-core), (3) initialize Grimoire (golem-grimoire), (4) start Heartbeat ticker (golem-core), (5) boot Safety layer (golem-safety), (6) enter event loop.
- Keep main() thin. Delegate subsystem startup to submodules or tasks spawned on the runtime.
- Error context propagates via `anyhow::Result<()>`; let it bubble up from startup steps.

## Test Requirements

- Integration tests should validate:
  - Binary compiles and executes without panic
  - Tracing is initialized; at least one info! message is logged
  - Exit code is 0 on success, non-zero on error
  - (Future) startup completes within a timeout; health checks pass
- Place tests in `tests/integration/` or `tests/e2e/` using `assert_cmd` or similar subprocess testing

## Do Not

- Do not initialize `tracing_subscriber` more than once in the same process (will panic)
- Do not add blocking I/O directly in main(); spawn it via `tokio::task::block_in_place()` or `spawn_blocking()`
- Do not remove `#[tokio::main]` or manually create a Runtime
- Do not make startup depend on external services (config files, network, database) without graceful degradation or fallback defaults
